welcome.script:
Hi, scientists! Welcome to the Field Station. Today you're solving a real mystery.

[ON SCREEN: CAM 1 beach · CAM 2 woods · CAM 3 river · CAM 4 marsh]
These pictures came from four trail cameras in Florida: a baby sea turtle, a panther, a manatee and a cottonmouth snake.

[ON SCREEN: The times]
Look at the clocks. All four animals moved within about two minutes, and the cameras were far apart. Hmm. I wonder why.

[ON SCREEN: The case question]
That's our case: what made them all react, and how did each one know?

[ON SCREEN: Your clue bar]
See "My clues" under the tabs? Every game you finish turns a question mark into a clue. Four clues cracks the case.

Type your first name on the ID card. Then press Listen on Dr. Reyes's walkie-talkie, right below me.

The moment you hear SNAP, tap fast.

parts.body: Write at least three steps, in order. Start with the sound. End with you turning around.

warmup.script:
Let's start with you, because your body does this too.

[ON SCREEN: The snap test]
Under the walkie-talkie is a game called "Hear the snap." Tap the picture, then wait. Don't guess! When you hear the snap, tap fast. Try it three times. Watch me.

(Do the test once on camera. Read your time out loud.)

I didn't stop and think. My body just did it!

[ON SCREEN: Your steps]
Then write what happened in your body, in order, from the sound to your tap. There are no wrong answers yet.

How did your body decide that fast? Press Listen and hear what Dr. Reyes thinks.

parts.label: 🔭 Word Lens

parts.body: Dr. Reyes reads the word and what it means. The words light up as she reads. Try to tap all six.

vocab.script:
Four of today's words are steps, so let's act them out. Stand up if you can!

[ON SCREEN: Stimulus]
Stimulus: something happens. (Snap your fingers.)

[ON SCREEN: Sense organ]
Sense organ: a body part notices it. (Point to your ear.)

[ON SCREEN: Brain]
Brain: it decides. (Tap your head.)

[ON SCREEN: Response]
Response: you do something. (Turn around.)

[ON SCREEN: Act it out]
Faster: snap, ear, head, turn! That's your snap test.

[ON SCREEN: Word Lens]
Now tap each word sticker below me. Dr. Reyes reads the word and what it means. Get a green check on all six.

lesson.script:
[ON SCREEN: This tab]
This tab has four parts and three clues. Part 1 teaches the four steps, then you play Send the Signal for clue two. Part 2 is about different senses, with an alligator picture. In Part 3 you open Dr. Reyes's four cameras for clue three. And in Part 4, one more camera shows a heron. Sort its steps for clue four. Go in order, and watch your clue bar.

part1.label: Part 1 · the four steps + Send the Signal

parts.label: 🔁 The four steps
parts.title: Every animal reaction
rows: Something happens in the world: a sound, a smell, a flash of light.
A body part picks it up: eyes, ears, nose, tongue or skin.
The brain decides what it means.

parts.label: 📡 Send the signal
parts.title: Put the steps in order
rows: Drag each step onto a station, or tap a step, then a station.
Start where the message starts: out in the world.
Fill all four and watch the signal run. That’s Clue 2!

part1.script:
Let's name what happened in your snap test.

[ON SCREEN: The four steps]
Every reaction has four steps, in order. A stimulus: the snap. A sense organ notices it: your ears. Your brain decides: "Something's behind me!" And the response: you tapped. All four can happen in less than one second!

Think about your warm-up list. Did you write a step for your brain? Lots of people skip it, because it's so fast.

[ON SCREEN: Send the signal]
Below the reading is Send the Signal. Drag each step onto a station, starting out in the world. Get all four right and watch the signal run. That's clue two!

First, press Listen. Dr. Reyes has something to say about the middle steps.

part2.label: Part 2 · different senses

parts.label: 👀 Five senses
parts.title: Each sense organ picks up something different
rows: touch, heat and cold, and pain

parts.label: ⚠ Watch out
parts.title: The brain can’t do it alone
parts.body: No sense organ, no signal. No signal, no response.

part2.script:
An eagle spots a fish with its eyes. A panther hears a rustle with its ears.

[ON SCREEN: Five senses]
Each sense organ picks up something different. Eyes pick up light, ears pick up sound, your nose picks up smell, your tongue picks up taste, and your skin picks up touch, heat and cold.

[ON SCREEN: Watch out]
Watch out for one mistake: the brain can't notice anything by itself. No sense organ, no signal. No signal, no response. Remember that for the end of the assignment.

figure.label: The alligator picture
figure.script:
[ON SCREEN: Alligator pathway]
Read this picture left to right, like a sentence.

[ON SCREEN: Read it left to right]
A splash: that's the stimulus. The alligator's ear: the sense organ. Its brain decides, "Food!" Then it turns toward the splash: the response. The yellow lines show the message traveling. Can you say all four steps without looking?

part3.label: Part 3 · open the four cameras (Clue 3)

parts.label: 📹 How to open a camera
parts.title: Open all four

part3.script:
Time to look at the evidence, like a real field scientist.

[ON SCREEN: How to open a camera]
Below the walkie-talkie are four trail cameras. Tap one, then press Next step to follow the message through that animal, one step at a time.

[ON SCREEN: CAM 1 beach]
For each one, ask: what started this reaction? Was it the same thing for all four? That's clue three.

[ON SCREEN: The manatee photo]
Then tap the numbers on the manatee photo to see how it feels the water.

Press Listen. Dr. Reyes will tell you what to watch for.

explore.label: Part 4 · the heron on CAM 5 (Clue 4)

parts.label: 📖 The heron story
parts.title: A heron hunting
parts.body: A great blue heron stands still in shallow water. A small fish swims into view. The heron freezes, then strikes. Its sharp beak grabs the fish.

parts.label: 🃏 One card, sorted
parts.title: A small fish swims into view.
rows: It happens out in the water, before the heron does anything. It starts everything.

parts.label: 🧠 The hidden step
parts.title: No camera can see it
parts.body: The brain step happens inside the heron. Keep it in mind: it’s great evidence for your CER.

explore.script:
[ON SCREEN: The heron]
CAM 5 caught a great blue heron hunting, one minute after the other cameras.

[ON SCREEN: The heron story]
Read the story slowly. The heron stands still. A fish swims by. The heron freezes, then strikes. I notice it froze first. I wonder why?

[ON SCREEN: One card, sorted]
Drag each card into its step. Let's do one together: "A small fish swims into view." That happens out in the water, before the heron does anything. So it's the stimulus! You sort the rest.

[ON SCREEN: The hidden step]
The pink box is the brain. No card goes there, because no camera can see inside the heron's head. Remember that for your CER.

Press Listen for Dr. Reyes.

[ON SCREEN: Self-Check]
This Self-Check isn't graded. It's just for you. Answer one question, then press Next question. Picked a wrong answer? Read the hint. It tells you what to think about. Think about the four steps, and try again.

assignment.script:
You made it to the assignment!

[ON SCREEN: Crack the case]
First, crack the case. Still locked? Tap "Show me where the clues are," then "Go there." With all four clues, pick the answer that fits every clue. Did all four animals react to the same thing?

[ON SCREEN: Today’s parts]
Then there are three parts. Part B: two answers in complete sentences. Part C: make up your own Florida animal moment. A sketch is a bonus. And last, a CER.

[ON SCREEN: Saved for you]
Everything saves itself and shows up in Gathered Answers at the bottom. That's what you turn in.

Press Listen. Dr. Reyes wants a real field report.

partb.script:
[ON SCREEN: Part B tools]
Answer three questions in complete sentences, using our step words. Under each box, the "Your answer needs" chips turn green as you include each part. Stuck? Press "Need a hint?" for one hint at a time. And "My evidence" adds anything you highlighted.

[ON SCREEN: CAM 1 beach · CAM 2 woods]
For question five, pick an animal from last night's cameras. They're right above the question.

parts.label: 🐾 Your scenario
parts.title: A made-up moment, like the heron story
rows: A Florida animal NOT in today’s lesson.
Pelican, bobcat, anole lizard, armadillo, dolphin…

parts.title: Draw, then label
rows: Draw your animal and what it noticed.
Drag from a part of your drawing to an empty spot, then type.
Show the order of the four steps.

partc.script:
Now you're the scientist.

[ON SCREEN: Your scenario]
Make up a short moment, like the heron story, about a Florida animal that wasn't in today's lesson. A pelican? A bobcat? A dolphin? Fill in the four boxes: what happened, what noticed it, what the brain decided, and what the animal did.

[ON SCREEN: The sketch pad]
If you have time, sketch it too. It's a bonus. Draw with the pen. To add a label, pick Label, drag from a part of your drawing to an empty spot, and type. Add arrows to show the order.

evidence.label: Use your evidence · CER

parts.label: 💬 The classmate says
parts.title: A classmate says…
parts.body: “Animals just react. They don’t really need a brain. Their senses do all the work.”

parts.label: ⚖ CER
parts.title: Claim · Evidence · Reasoning
rows: Claim: what you think is true.
Evidence: facts from the lesson that prove it.
Reasoning: how the facts prove your claim.

evidence.script:
[ON SCREEN: The classmate says]
A classmate says, "Animals just react. They don't really need a brain. Their senses do all the work." Hmm. Think about the hidden pink box from the heron. Do you agree?

[ON SCREEN: CER]
Remember CER: your claim, your evidence from today's lesson, and your reasoning.

[ON SCREEN: The planner]
Tap "I agree" or "I disagree," then tap two pieces of evidence. They drop right into your boxes! The reasoning is all you. Try starting with "This shows that…"

closing.script:
[ON SCREEN: Case closed · Confetti]
Case closed! You did it, scientists.

Four animals noticed four different things with four different senses, and each one's brain decided what to do. The four steps solved it.

[ON SCREEN: Before you go]
Two last things. Check every box in What to Turn In to earn a heron feather. And download your field journal.

[ON SCREEN: Next time]
Press Listen. Dr. Reyes has a sneak peek at next time.

vr.script:
Hi, scientists! Dr. Reyes has a problem. Her radio log from the panther night is full of static.

[ON SCREEN: The radio log]
Every message is missing steps. (Hold up four fingers.) Remember the four: stimulus, sense organ, brain, response.

[ON SCREEN: Two ways]
Pick your way at the top. With a headset, you’ll go inside a giant brain! Put a panther there and build four sense stations around it. Say the four steps out loud at each one.

[ON SCREEN: The bear strip]
No headset? You’ll make three comic strips, like this bear sniffing berries, one panel for each step.

[ON SCREEN: The badge]
Finish in VR and you earn the Golden Antenna badge!

Press Listen on Dr. Reyes’s walkie-talkie, right below me.
